idiom_name: class with a #private array, [Symbol.iterator]() and frozen copies on read
implementation_notes: JavaScript offers no collection base class and no runtime read-only view, so the structure is hand-written: hold the array in a #private field (privacy enforced by the language, not by convention), expose add/remove as methods that check the invariants, and implement [Symbol.iterator]() (or a values() generator) so for...of, spread and destructuring keep working. Reads return a copy - typically Object.freeze([...this.#items]) for a defensive snapshot - because neither private fields nor freeze make the elements immutable, and freezing the internal array in place would break the collection's own mutations. Avoid `class Orders extends Array`: subclassed built-ins carry species and extra-index traps and still publish every mutating Array method.
pitfalls: Private fields are per-class: a subclass cannot read #items, so extension by subclassing does not work - extend by delegation instead.
Object.freeze is shallow and only protects the copy's own slots: mutate an element through the returned array and the collection changes with it.
Any method that returns this.#items, or the result of push/splice, leaks the container and with it the invariants.
JSON.stringify ignores private fields, so the collection serializes as {} unless toJSON() is provided.
